title: Differentiation of Trigonometric Functions
summary: d/dx sin x = cos x; cos x → −sin x; tan x → sec²x; cot x → −cosec²x; sec x → sec x tan x; cosec x → −cosec x cot x (x in radians).
If x is in degrees, x° = πx/180, so d/dx(cot x°) = −(π/180) cosec²x°.
d/dx sin⁻¹x = 1/√(1 − x²); cos⁻¹x → −1/√(1 − x²); tan⁻¹x → 1/(1 + x²); cot⁻¹x → −1/(1 + x²); sec⁻¹x → 1/(|x|√(x² − 1)).
d/dx sin³x = 3 sin²x cos x. d/dx sin⁻¹(x²) = 2x/√(1 − x⁴). d/dx √(sin³x) = (3/2)√(sin x) cos x.
Simplify first when possible: sin⁻¹(cos x) = π/2 − x, so its derivative is −1.
mcq: The derivative of y = sin³x with respect to x is —
If y = sin 2x cos 3x, then dy/dx is —

mcq.work: sin⁻¹(cos x) = sin⁻¹(sin(π/2 − x)) = π/2 − x (0 ≤ x ≤ π) ⇒ dy/dx = −1.

objective: Fill in the blanks: (a) If y = √(sin³x), then dy/dx = ______. (b) If y = sin⁻¹(x²), then dy/dx = ______.
vsa: If cos y = x cos(a + y), prove that dy/dx = cos²(a + y)/sin a.

x = cos y/cos(a + y). dx/dy = [−sin y cos(a + y) + cos y sin(a + y)]/cos²(a + y) = sin(a + y − y)/cos²(a + y) = sin a/cos²(a + y).
So dy/dx = cos²(a + y)/sin a.
Differentiate x sin x + cos x with respect to x.
(1·sin x + x cos x) − sin x = x cos x.
sa: If y = sin⁻¹x, show that (1 − x²) d²y/dx² − x dy/dx = 0.

dy/dx = 1/√(1 − x²) ⇒ √(1 − x²) y' = 1.
Differentiate: √(1 − x²) y'' + y'(−x/√(1 − x²)) = 0.
Multiply by √(1 − x²): (1 − x²)y'' − xy' = 0.
